column1: # Marker-text audit: every numbered "Deciphering the Icon" marker read against the picture
# under its own circle, at full size, with crops where the detail is small.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The reading audit (icon_reading_audit.tsv) finished 2026-09-21 and
# examined MARKER TEXT on only the 48 icons it touched that day; roughly one marker in three
# on those was wrong. The other 65 icons — the rows marked checked-2026-08-21b and
# checked-2026-08-22 there — had their PROSE read against the picture and their MARKER TEXTS
# never examined by anyone. This file is that sweep. 65 icons, 347 markers.
# A ROW HERE MEANS NOTHING UNLESS hotspots.js / hotspots3.js SAYS WHAT THE NOTE SAYS. The
# reading audit's 28 fixed-2026-08-22 rows recorded corrections that were never applied to
# the source, and the reader shipped the wrong text for a month. Every `fixed` row below was
# written AFTER the edit landed and AFTER grepping the old wording out of the source.
# One row per MARKER, not per icon — per-icon rows are how 47 bad marker texts hid behind 65

column5: note   (verdict: holds | fixed-DATE)

he does not recline and his hand is not raised: he sits upright on a cushioned seat and his right hand is down at his knee, fingers reaching toward the woman. Prose in hotspots2.js said 'reclines' too and was fixed with it
position right, but her hair is bound under a white cloth — nothing is wiped with it. Added what is there: face turned up, hands at his bare foot
the vase is there and upright, two-handled and white, standing on the pavement below the couch; the prose called it 'emptied on the floor', which the picture does not show
a press of eight or nine unhaloed heads at the right, two hands legible in gesture over the table
one footed bowl at the centre of the cloth, with round loaves, long loaves and green sprigs about it
the robe is not plain — a dark red mantle over a gold-shot green brocade sleeve; hand flat on the table edge is right, and the column that sets him apart is now named
'seated' cannot be seen — the table cuts him at the waist; he is at the centre behind it in a yellow hood and veil, both hands down on the cloth
not a heap: the coins lie spread flat in one layer under both his hands
caps and hoods, not turbans; one elder seated in orange in front and a beardless young man in blue among them

column3: The canopy and the drawn curtain
column5: a red velum swagged between the flanking buildings and gathered at both columns, over a gabled central portico

column3: Christ at the head of the table
column5: cruciform halo confirmed at full crop, but no bread is painted on this table: the blessing hand is at his breast, the left hand reaches over the cloth
ὁ δεῖπνος left of the hanging lamp, ὁ μυστικός right of it — both read at full crop
'the only beardless face among the twelve' is false — at least two more beardless apostles on the right side; and he is bowed forward at the Lord's side, not leaning back
an arm comes in from the right and the fingers are over the rim of the central basin
not bread and a cup: a footed basin at the centre with a dark flask, two small cups and knives — the icon's own prose reading said so and the marker contradicted it
upper left, reclining, the one gold halo in the panel (abraded); his hand is over the bowed disciple at his breast
bowed small and close under the Lord's chin, head almost on the table

column3: The hand stretched to the dish
column5: the reach is more exact than the text said: the hand comes down INTO a small footed cup on the cloth, which is the dipping itself
two footed cups, a lidded vessel and triangular wedges all lie in full view on the tilted top
counted twice at full crop: TWELVE apostles, not eleven — seven behind the table and five seated in front with their backs half turned
a gabled building at each upper corner with a plain wall between them
read at full crop: ΗΑΡΝΗCΙC ΤȢ ΠΕΤΡȢ, lunate sigmas and an ou-ligature — the denial of Peter
the company at the fire is two soldiers in scale armour and helmets and a young man in blue, not servants, and Peter sits apart across the flames from them
a girl in red in the doorway with her right hand up, pointing at him
'another maid names him again' is not in the picture — the fresco paints one maid and repeats Peter instead
he is not sitting with his face in his hands: he is bent double over a green column with his face buried in his arms

not a wall above him: the flat roof of a small white building beside him, and the bird's head is thrown back with the beak open, crowing. Prose in hotspots2.js called it 'a little pillared roof' and said 'two moments' where the wall paints three; fixed with it

column3: Christ at prayer on the rock
column5: upper left, haloed, bowed deep over the rock
four figures of Christ on this wall, not three prayers: two bowed, one upright at the top centre, one turned back to the sleepers — which is what the icon's own prose reading already said
haloed, head inclined, right hand out and down toward the sleepers
not 'the three' — about a dozen figures fill the whole foot of the wall, the eight told to sit here as well as the three taken farther on
the rock is ochre and pale olive where the light falls; only the crags along the top are near-black. 'grey and black' described no part of it
the titulus is longer than the marker gave: Η ΠΡΟΣΕΥΧΗ ΤΟΥ ΧΥ, the Prayer of Christ. ΙΣ ΧΣ beside each figure confirmed
far left, kneeling on the rock, both hands stretched out to the right
three kneeling figures of Christ across the left two-thirds of the wall, a fourth standing at the right
standing over the sleepers in dark red, right hand out and down
both hands are open toward the Lord, not one, and he is the grey-haired one
about eleven heads heaped at the foot of the rock, wrapped and inert

the fresco paints Luke's angel — a small winged haloed figure high in the dark sky — and no marker or reading had ever named it. Added to the prose; a marker there would clamp to 9% and land on Christ's halo
…LATE 7 OR… / …TIS IN TEM… legible at full crop, with a Tironian 7 for ET; the left half of the band is too worn to read in this photograph

column3: The angel out of the gold
column5: it does not come head-first: it flies in level from the left with its hand stretched out to meet Christ's, and carries no cup
kneeling on the hill, both hands lifted toward the angel
he stands upright, not bending, and holds a closed scroll in his left hand — the scroll was in no text
heaped across the middle and the whole lower left of the panel
ΗΠΡΟΔΟCΙΑ read across the top
green tunic, one arm across the body and the other hand on the far shoulder, face to face, no halo
cruciform halo confirmed at full crop, still, one hand down

MISPLACED as well as wrong: the sword at the left belongs to the arresting party, not to a disciple. Peter and Malchus are at the LOWER RIGHT — marker moved from 48%/27% to 76%/85% and the text rewritten to what is painted there
there is also an axe and a white gabled lantern with the flame inside it, held up on a staff, against a black sky pricked with stars
the man laying hands on him wears no armour — a beardless youth in a plain red tunic with a dagger at his belt; the armoured soldier stands behind him
·RADITIO· at the left of the band and DOMI[NI] at the right, both read at full crop
his face is set straight forward, NOT turned to the man kissing him; cruciform halo confirmed
one arm round him, not both — the other hand reaching across the Lord belongs to someone else in the press
bottom left, Peter grips the servant's head and holds the blade at his ear, the servant down on the ground
a lantern AND a hanging lamp on poles, and two long axes and a knobbed club among the spears

he wears no cuirass and no armour — a pointed cap and a mantle over a white tunic. The 'one Roman in armour, and the state behind the council' was not in the picture; label changed to 'The man at the right edge'
the halo is deep orange-red and the cross in it is faint, not the clean cruciform the text implied; and his hands are not visible at all, so 'one hand at his side' was invented
leans in from the left, face against the Lord's cheek, arm across him
spears, two axe-heads and a curved blade raised in a line across the top
right, and better than it said: the monogram ΙΣ ΧΣ is lettered either side of the lantern's pole over the Lord's head

nobody is struck in this fresco — no servant on the ground, no ear. A man in red holds a sword raised over his head, and nothing identifies him as a disciple. Label changed to 'The raised sword at the left'
there are no helmets and no armour anywhere in the panel; every head is bare. Label changed to 'The bare heads of the crowd'
Ο Χ͞C ΚΡΙΝΟΜΕΝΟC ΥΠΟ ΑΝΝΑ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΙΑΦΑ read at full crop; the marker expands the nomen sacrum, which is fair
and better than the text said — both hands have the tunic pulled apart at the breast and the pale undergarment shows through
right, and his raised open hand toward the prisoner was left unsaid
haloed, standing before the seated judges
no book and no lectern: a white sheet of imitation script and a black inkwell on a low yellow table
no cuirass and no spear in his hands — a green belted tunic, laced red leggings, arms folded, a shaft leaning behind him
his hand is not lifted toward the accused: the front of his robe is painted as a mass of torn strips with his hand at the tear — Gračanica paints the rending, the verdict, not the question
a man in red between the seat and the prisoner with his arm thrown out toward Christ
standing, haloed, head bowed, wrapped in the mantle with no hands showing
helmeted, in tunic and cape with a sword at his side, his hand at Christ's arm
a group of pale-robed men behind the guard at the right edge
right, and now says what is there: the cock stands on the crown of the arch with lettering either side of it on the black ground
ΥΠΕCΤΡΕΨΕ ΤΑ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΑ read across the top
red mantle over a teal tunic, bent over the table with his hand down among the coins
no cloth — a bare yellow table-top, and beside the coins an open written scroll, a reed pen and a black inkwell that no text mentioned. Label changed to 'The silver on the table'
the crowned one seated at the end of the table and a second seated beyond him, neither rising, a press of heads behind
right, and the fresco letters his name ΙȢΔΑС beside his head, and dresses him in the same red mantle as at the table — neither was said

the buildings are not identified as the temple by anything in the picture: a pink enclosure wall and a green red-roofed building with its door open, and a small figure in a red hood leaning over the parapet to watch
one tree with a spreading crown and nothing else growing in the field
the cord runs from the branch down behind the head to the neck; the face is fully painted, thrown back, mouth open
pale rock in steps, no building and no other figure
only the right hand is legible, open and half curled; the left is lost in the folds, so 'the hands' was one hand too many
no feet are in the photograph at all — the wall curves away below the hem. Label changed to 'Where the picture ends'
the fresco writes ΑΠΟΝΗΨΙС with an eta, not ΑΠΟΝΙΨΙΣ, and the ΙΣ ΧΣ is in the sky above the halo, not beside it
crowned, on a raised seat, both hands out over the basin
and the same soldier in lamellar armour holds the basin under his hands; the water is a thin painted arc
cruciform halo, head bowed, both hands held loose before him, unbound
the head is uncovered and the hair bound up — Orthodox painting veils its women, so the figure cannot simply be called Pilate's wife; the marker now says what is there and why readers take it for her
a press of bearded elders from the right, the front one with his hand raised
'hands crossed in front of him' cannot be seen on this darkened panel; one hand comes forward at the waist. The point that stands is that nothing binds him
three helmets, and spear shafts above them, which the text left out
crowned, seated on the wooden throne in a gold-banded robe, arm out toward the accused
one white headcloth and one gold cap; the two in front are bare-headed, so 'turbans and caps' overstated it
a beardless servant behind the throne-back, bent forward, a dark oval vessel held at his chest
a wide platform in flat red and pale bands under the seat
